claim: Insight is defined by solver self-report after a correct solve. About 56% of correct solves are labelled insight in three independent designs (CRA EEG N=19: 56%; anagrams N=26: 56.1%; 2024 EEG N=21: 55.6%). Eureka is also reported on 22.7% of incorrect trials (2024 study), so the label is not tied to correctness. An LLM version needs a behavioural proxy. Gap 7 update: a 2026 study (N=377) found Aha ratings highest for solutions with a correct first move, not for restructured ones, so the label tracks correctness and style.
agent_test: Not a neural claim. Test a proxy (sudden answer change after a long impasse) against held-out correctness at equal tokens.

claim: The founding EEG study found a right-temporal (T8) gamma burst about 0.3 s before the insight button press (t(18)=3.48, p=.003; insight x window x hemisphere F(1,18)=8.11, p=.011) and an earlier right posterior alpha burst (9.8 Hz). One lab, N=19, no independent replication found. Gap 1 update: still no independent replication of the burst timing. Kounios 2006 could not separate its gamma effects from EMG; a 2023 perceptual EEG study (N=25, cluster-corrected) found no gamma difference; gamma tACS (N=31) raised CRA accuracy but tests stimulation, not the burst.
agent_test: No online neural signal in a model. Analogy only: look for a late sharp confidence or entropy jump before the final answer and measure whether it predicts correctness.

claim: Sandkuhler and Bhattacharya found parieto-occipital gamma (38-44 Hz) for sudden vs non-sudden solutions (302 vs 88 trials pooled, N=21). This is only a partial replication of the gamma finding: different design (hints, impasse), different scalp site and time window, and alpha read as suppression of solution information, not vision gating.
agent_test: None directly.

claim: fMRI evidence for right anterior temporal activity in insight is thin and mixed. Jung-Beeman 2004 (N=13, 0.25% peak, 531 mm3) and Subramaniam 2009 (N=10, right temporal pole 164 voxels, but deactivated) vs Tik 2018 (N=29, left not right) and the 2024 EEG (left not right, N=21).
agent_test: None. Do not build a hemisphere-based module.

claim: Pooled fMRI meta-analyses find insight effects in inferior and middle frontal, parahippocampal and amygdala regions, not a right anterior temporal core, and the pattern depends on the insight task type. Two of the three sources were read at abstract level only.
agent_test: None.

claim: Brain stimulation of the right anterior temporal lobe is inconsistent: Chi and Snyder 2011 (60% vs 20% solved the hardest matchstick problem, p=.022, about 20 per group) and a 2020 study (partial eta-squared .06) vs Aihara 2017 (N=66, no significant effect). Gap 9 update: Aihara 2017 had N=66 within-subject, g=-0.19 (CI -0.69 to 0.30) so a small positive effect is not excluded; the hard matchstick part was underpowered (3 solvers); Salvi 2020 (HD-tDCS, N=36 per group, positive) and Santarnecchi 2019 (40 Hz tACS, N=31, positive, some p values inconsistent) are not independent of the founding framework. Inconclusive, not shown absent.
agent_test: None.

claim: A resting-state trait difference exists: people who solve more anagrams with insight show different resting EEG (alpha, beta, gamma) but equal accuracy and RT (N=26; correct 68.9% vs 70.9%; RT 5.19 vs 5.10 s). Single lab, median split, partly uncorrected follow-ups.
agent_test: Analogy: vary the model's prompt style or sampling spread (broad vs focused) and test which problems each solves at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM paper found that tests an EEG-style or hemisphere signature of insight; the literature search for it came back empty (limited by shared search budget).
agent_test: None needed; this is an absence claim.

claim: Spontaneous mid-reasoning Aha shifts in LLMs are rare (6.31% of traces over 1M+ traces) and do not help: Qwen2.5-1.5B 2.57% correct with a shift vs 16.44% without (N=723,200); a strict Aha detector fires on 1.79%. Shift label is an LLM judge (kappa about 0.73).
agent_test: Count self-reported mid-trace shifts in our agent's traces; compare accuracy with and without a shift at equal tokens. Do not treat a shift as a success signal.

claim: Externally triggered reconsideration under high entropy improves accuracy: the cue 'Wait, we need to reconsider' raised MATH-500 from 32.21% to 40.62% (+8.41 pp; 50,574 wins vs 23,500 losses); gain near zero on crosswords (+0.45 pp) and Rush Hour (+0.01 pp). Model dependence (gap 3): forced reconsideration on a MATH subset gave +5.97 pp for Qwen2.5-7B but -4.19 pp for Llama 3.1-8B.
agent_test: Trigger forced reconsideration only when token entropy or answer disagreement is high; compare with always-trigger and never-trigger at equal tokens.

claim: The R1-style Aha moment is mostly decorative or rare under several measures: under 10% of VLM responses show aha with marginal gain; over 30% of steps in some large models are decorative (true-thinking score under 0.005); keyword reflection detection is noisy.
agent_test: Prune low-contribution steps and measure accuracy at lower token count; check self-verification against an independent verifier.

claim: Models fail verification more than generation on insight-like riddles: verification failures are 5% to 39% of wrong answers (201 Japanese riddles, 38 models; reasoning models 17.6% vs non-reasoning 7.6%; humans 52.9%). Gap 8 update: the paper only proposes structured verification; no independent-checker test exists in the sources found.
agent_test: Add a separate answer-check step on riddle-type items and measure the gain at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are fixated by decoys: GPT-4 solved 6 Only Connect walls on the original set, 59 with decoys diluted and 471 with decoys removed (494 test walls). Visual-RAT models echo literal image content in 22.8% of wrong answers vs 8.9% for humans.
agent_test: Add a step that lists the surface features driving the current answer and asks for an answer avoiding them; test on decoy-rich items at equal tokens.

claim: Semantic-distance tests do not predict LLM creativity once general ability is controlled: RAT validity r=+0.62 falls to +0.08..+0.28 (55 models, 30 items); DAT vs Hivemind r=+0.30 falls to -0.01.
agent_test: Do not use RAT score as a creativity proxy; test on held-out creative-writing judgements.

claim: Re-inserting key intermediate conclusions (Insight Replay, 3 rounds) gave +1.65 points average over chain of thought across 24 settings (largest +9.2 on R1-Distill-32B LiveCodeBench). The paper's insight is not the neuroscience concept.
agent_test: Replay the stored key conclusions at the final-answer step at equal tokens.

claim: A heuristic search model over a free-association network matches human RAT accuracy (Pearson r=0.742 over 138 items), supporting an associative-search account with no hemisphere-specific mechanism; the 2024 EEG found association strength predicts accuracy (beta=.11) but remoteness had no EEG cluster.
agent_test: Implement an association-graph search for remote-associate items and compare with free generation at equal tokens.

claim: Bowden and Jung-Beeman 2003 (N=44) is behavioural. Solution words rated insightful were primed more after unsolved problems; the left-visual-field (RH) advantage was 33 ms, F(1,43)=4.4, p=.04 (priming 70 vs 39 ms). Authors say both hemispheres cooperate. Kounios 2006 (EEG N=19, fMRI N=25) shows a pre-problem brain state: 56.2% and 55.8% of solutions labelled insight.
agent_test: No agent test; background only.

claim: No source found shows a sharp confidence or entropy jump just before correct LLM answers on RAT or riddle items. The nearest evidence (math, Qwen3 1.7B-8B) says correct traces have smooth falling entropy and incorrect traces have unresolved spikes.
agent_test: On RAT items, log token entropy per step and test whether a late spike or smoothness predicts correctness better than chance and better than self-consistency, at equal tokens.

claim: The 2601.00514 findings (rare shifts, forced reconsideration helps under high entropy) were measured only on Qwen2.5 and Llama (small, GRPO-tuned) over math, crosswords and Rush Hour. Nothing found tests closed or frontier models or insight-type items. Gaps 3 and 5 are open.
agent_test: Replicate the entropy-gated reconsideration on RAT, riddles and matchsticks with a larger open model, at equal tokens against best-of-N.

claim: A riddle-style rewrite test (Riddle Riddle, 9 LLMs, 100 humans): LLMs 84.9% on genuine riddles vs 50.7% on literal riddle riddles; humans 50.5% vs 80.5%; 90.8% of LLM errors on riddle riddles came from over-inventive reasoning. An insight or restructure step can hurt when the literal reading is right.
agent_test: Gate any decoy-listing or restructure step behind a failed literal attempt; test on both riddles and literal control items.
